title: [testintro] Add a test-introspection tool
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #187756
* #187755
* __->__ #187754

WARNING: AI Slop ahead - this was entirely vibe-coded and I mostly reviewed the design and methodology rather than the code itself.

---
Add tools/testing/introspection/, which enumerates the concrete tests a CI target
(platform/config) generates -- by importing test files under a small, centralized
device-capability descriptor monkeypatched on top of the real (current) torch
build, rather than running them on the target hardware -- and diffs that test set
between two git refs or for a PR. This is the engine behind the test-diff PR
comment (#187755).

Simulating the descriptor (cpu/cuda/mps/xpu) lets one CPU build answer for every
platform, so generated/synthetic tests (instantiate_device_type_tests, ops,
parametrize, copy_tests) are enumerated exactly; results match
`pytest --collect-only` on representative files, and a missing descriptor probe
fails loudly rather than producing wrong output.

Suggested review order: platforms.py (Platform/Config/Job model), collector.py
(descriptor + test harvesting + content-hash cache), diff.py (the added/removed
diff), then test_introspection.py.

The standalone `testintro` CLI and its `where`/`list` behaviors are split into a
follow-up PR; collector.py still carries the gut-and-run "status" harvesting they
use (interwoven with the worker), but this PR exercises only the enumerate path
the diff needs.

Authored by Claude.
